st: Season the chicken with salt. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove it to a plate.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same oil for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, then add the blended tomatoes and whole chili. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick and the oil rises to the top.
Return the chicken to the pot, add [[1 cup]] hot water, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Lift out the chicken and keep warm.
Add [[2 cups]] hot water to the sauce and bring it to a boil. Remove the chili.
Lower the heat and add the corn flour a handful at a time, stirring hard with a wooden spoon so no lumps form.
Keep cooking and pressing the paste against the pot for 8 to 10 minutes until it is thick, smooth and pulls away from the sides.
Serve the red paste in mounds with the chicken on top.
Season the fish with salt and set aside.
Heat the palm oil in a pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 8 minutes until they form a thick sauce.
Pour in [[2 cups]] water, add the chili and okra, and bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 12 minutes until the okra is tender and the sauce is slippery and thick.
Lay the fish chunks on top, cover, and cook gently for 6 to 8 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes at 145°F (63°C).
Taste for salt and serve hot with pate, rice or cornmeal paste.
Blend the tomatoes, half of the onion and the chili until smooth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the remaining chopped onion for 4 minutes until soft.
Pour in the blended tomato mixture and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and darkens.
Season with salt and stir in the lemon juice.
Serve warm or cool as a sauce for fried or grilled fish.
Grind the peanuts in a food processor for several minutes until they form a thick, oily paste.
Scrape the paste into a bowl and knead it with your hands, squeezing out the oil into a separate dish and pouring off the extra.
Add the ginger, cayenne, onion powder and salt and knead until evenly mixed.
Work in [[2 tbsp]] warm water, a little at a time, until the dough is firm and holds together.
Roll the dough into thin sticks or small rings, each about as thick as a pencil.
Heat the peanut oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the pieces in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until golden brown and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and cool completely so they become crunchy. Store in a sealed jar.
Put the black-eyed peas in a pot with [[4 cups]] water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, for 35 to 40 minutes until just tender.
Drain the peas, saving the cooking liquid. Add water to make [[3.5 cups]] of liquid.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until golden.
Stir in the tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 8 minutes until thick.
Add the rice and cooked peas and stir for 2 minutes to coat them in the sauce.
Pour in the measured liquid and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 18 minutes until the rice is tender.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork and serve.
Season the chicken with salt. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken for 4 minutes per side. Remove it.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pot with the whole chili and [[3 cups]] hot water. Simmer, covered, for 25 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C).
Whisk the peanut butter with [[2 cups]] hot water until smooth, then stir it into the pot.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until the soup is thick and the oil rises to the top.
Season with salt and serve hot with rice or boiled yam.
